ranking.why: Rank by the worst profit per $100 that is still plausible, not by raw P&L. One imaginary total loss is added to every track (the disaster we may not have seen yet), and the bar is raised for testing many tracks at once, so lucky streaks do not top the board.

real_size.why: Paper trades are 5 shares (~$5). Real money ($300-500 in one strategy) means $10-$100 a trade, which eats deeper into the order book. Every paper fill is also re-priced on the same live book at these stakes (records only, never changes what a track trades). The trust ranking uses rank_size_usd.

late_fill.why: Each buy is re-priced on a fresh book this many seconds later, as if the order had landed late. Records only.

kc_maker.label: Kalshi late favorite (Reddit bot): in the last ~5 minutes of Kalshi's 15-minute BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP/DOGE/HYPE/BNB up-or-down windows, rests a buy order one tick in front of the best bid on the side that's winning (95c+), held to the result. Maker, no fee. Fills from the real trade tape after the close, behind anyone already waiting at that price. $10 an order, $100 paper

kc_maker_safe.label: Kalshi late favorite + spot check: same as kc_maker, but only when Binance spot sits at least 2 'typical moves until the close' past the strike on the winning side (the backtest's best family: +$0.56 per $100, band +$0.41 to +$0.73). $100 paper

kc_maker_safe_usd.label: Twin of kc_maker_safe with a price-gap check (12 Nov, Jan said yes): same rule, but the 2-typical-moves check must also pass after moving Binance onto Kalshi's price (Binance quotes in USDT and runs about 0.09% higher). History: half the losses, same +$0.57 per $100, about 25 in 100 fewer bets (backtest/kcloss.md). $100 paper

kc_maker_early.label: STOPPED 12 Nov (Jan: dump it). Kalshi favorite, earlier: one tick in front of the best bid on the winning side (90c+) with 6.5-11.5 minutes left instead of the last 5 (backtest: 7-10 minutes left did better than the last 1-3). $100 paper
kc_maker_early.stopped: 2026-11-12: Jan said dump it. Lost $79.62 on 341 bets (-$2.45 per $100), worse than luck explains (research/kalshi-tracks-review-2026-11-12.md). No new bids; open bets settle; history kept.

mirror_unlimited.label: Mirror, no cash limit: does he have an edge, and how much money would copying him need?

panic_fade.label: Panic fade (wildcard): buys the boring side right after a news scare knocks it down 6c+ in a day, sells when it recovers. $50 paper, refilled if it busts

arb.label: Arbitrage: Kalshi vs Polymarket, reviewed twin markets only, both legs bought, held to the end. $300 paper

endgame.label: Endgame: buys the winning side at 95-99c in markets that are decided but not paid out yet (result submitted, deadline passed, or ending within a day). Holds to payout. $100 paper

mention_no.label: Won't say it: in 'Will X say Y' markets ending within 7 days, buys NO at 25-90c. YES in these markets won less often than its price said (backtest/calib.md). One bet per event, real order-book fills. $50 paper

boring_no.label: Boring No, far out: in everyday 'will this happen' markets (no crypto, weather, elections and so on) with more than 30 days left, buys NO at 90-97c. In the history 100 of 101 such bets won (backtest/winners.md), found by looking, so this is a live test. One bet per event, real order-book fills. $500 paper, because each bet is stuck for a month or more

crypto_no.label: Crypto won't get there: in 'will Bitcoin reach / dip to / be above $X' markets with 3-7 days left, buys NO at 70-90c. In the history it was ahead in all 9 months (backtest/winners.md), but that could be luck, so this is a live test. One bet per event, real order-book fills. $50 paper

soccer_draw.label: Soccer draws: buys YES on 'will this game end in a draw' about 24h before kickoff when the draw costs 15-50c. In 4,538 past games draws won a bit more often than their price said (about 2c a bet, backtest/digs_draws.md). One bet per game, real order-book fills. $50 paper

postcount_no.label: UNTESTED (added 2026-11-12). Post counts, buy NO: in 'how many posts will Elon Musk / Trump / the White House make' markets, a counter (posts so far + what the same days brought in the last 8 weeks) says how likely each count range is. Where the Yes price is 10c or more above the counter, buys No (only when No costs 10c or more). History: +$4.16 per $100 on 825 bets, 'Promising, needs more bets', thin (backtest/tweets.md). One bet per market, real order-book fills. $100 paper

word_no.label: UNTESTED (added 2026-11-13). Word record, buy NO: in 'will X say Y' markets, checks how often that word really came up in the same speaker's earlier markets. Where the Yes price is 20c or more above that record (3+ earlier markets needed), buys No at 10-90c, at least 6 hours before the listed end. History since April: +$15.25 per $100 on 533 bets, 'Promising, needs more bets', no fresh test set (backtest/mentions.md). One bet per market, real order-book fills. $100 paper

stock_no.label: UNTESTED (added 2026-11-13). Stock long shots, buy NO: in 'will Nvidia close above $X' style markets, when Yes is listed at 5-25c with 1.5 to 4.5 hours left before the stock market closes, buys No, held to the close. History: +$5.33 per $100 on 339 bets (corrected 13 Nov: 33 of those bets bought No under 70c, prices the live track never takes, and made half the profit; the 254 bets bought at 75-95c, like the live track, made +$2.60 per $100, exam verdict Ahead, but could be luck) at one way of pricing the buy, -$5.58 at a harsher one, so only real asking prices can tell (backtest/stocks_comb.md). One bet per market, real order-book fills. $100 paper

quiet_no.label: Quiet week, buy NO: markets ending in 1-3 days whose price barely moved all week (less than 2c), buys NO at 50-75c. fade_sure.label: Fade the sure thing: in weather markets that end within a day, buys the CHEAP side (2-10c) when the other side looks 'sure' at 90-98c. Most bets lose; the few that win pay 10-50x. Real order-book fills. $25 paper

econ_fav.label: Forecast backs the favorite (added 2026-11-09): Kalshi CPI, jobless-claims, unemployment and jobs-report markets. 20-76 hours before the release, buys the side that costs 80-99c when a free forecast (Cleveland Fed for inflation, last release for the jobs numbers) says it is worth 3c+ more. Holds to the result. Real order-book fills. $50 paper

kalshi_patient.label: UNTESTED, added 2026-11-12. Kalshi patient buyer on the nearly-sure side: once an hour, where the likely side's best buy order is at 90-97c with a 2c+ gap to the asking price, it leaves a $10 buy order 1c above the best one for about an hour. Sports only before the game, no 15-minute crypto. Counts only contracts really sold to it on Kalshi's trade list. One bet per market, held to the result. History: +$0.61 per $100 on 1,275 bets over three samples (+$1.42 on the two it was found in, -$1.99 on a fresh third), could be luck (backtest/khouse.md). $1,000 paper, no refills

sharp_pinnacle.label: Sharp bookie price: buys a Polymarket game outcome (soccer, NBA/NHL/NFL, baseball, esports, MMA) when it costs at least 3c less than Pinnacle's odds say it's worth, after removing Pinnacle's margin and paying the fee. Pre-game only, holds to the end. Real order-book fills. $100 paper

every_horse.label: Buy every horse: buys every outcome of one multi-candidate market when together they cost less than the guaranteed payout after fees. All-YES only on provably complete lists; all-NO is safe either way. $100 paper

maker.label: STOPPED 12 Nov 2026 (lost money every way we tried; Jan said dump them). kc_maker.why: 2026-11-09, Jan's ask: test the Reddit '$50 to $3,000 on Kalshi 15-minute crypto' bot. Inferred method: a few minutes before a 15-minute window closes, rest a buy order on the side that's winning and hold it to the result. Makers pay no fee on these series (fee_type quadratic, checked 2026-11-09). Paper fills from the real trade tape after the close: a full fill only if something traded below our price, otherwise only sells at our price after the queue that was ahead of us. Backtest: kcrypto.py, backtest/kcrypto.md. Claude's track, rule changes reported.

maker.why: Polymarket pays about $190k a day to market makers. A slow bot can only keep it if the rewards beat the losses from getting picked off; this measures both.

claude.why: Sandbox (Jan, 2026-11-11): Claude may change these rules, 1-2 small changes a day, each logged in backtest/claude_changes.md. Change 1: the old 85-94c, 10-60 days, sell at 97c / 70c lost about $8 per $100 in history. Now the No side at 90-97c, 30-60 days left, a random pick among those, held to the end (history: about -$4 per $100, half the old loss).

panic_fade.why: Crowds overreact to scary headlines. If the boring side of a deadline market was 82c+ and fell 6c+ in a day without anything resolving, buy it and sell when it climbs back to where it was.

arb.why: Buy YES on one site and NO on the other when both together cost less than $1 after both sites' fees. Only on pairs whose rules were read side by side and approved (arb_pairs.json). Hold both legs to resolution.

endgame.why: Money comes back in hours or days instead of months. The risk is a 'sure thing' that flips or gets disputed; each trade records which signal it used so we learn which ones are safe.
endgame.tiers_note: 2026-11-08 (Jan's OK, after backtest/report.md): ending_soon dropped (lost about $5-6 per $100, mostly weather, crypto-price and tweet-count buckets at 95c a day before the end), then past_deadline dropped (lost $167 on 709 bets). Lab variants keep their own frozen tier lists.

every_horse.why: Exactly one outcome of a complete list wins, so one share of every YES pays exactly $1; one share of every NO pays (n-1) dollars, or n if an unlisted outcome wins, so the NO version needs no completeness.

ladder.why: If market A's YES can only happen when market B's YES does (same event, same rules text, only the strike or deadline differs), NO(A) + YES(B) always pays at least $1. Families are found daily and kept only if the words give a clear direction and the crowd's prices agree with it.

wallet_copy.why: Copy a wallet's new positions 5 shares each, sell when it sells. Skips crumbs (< $20 positions), late copies (our price more than 5c above its average) and caps at 10 new copies a day per wallet so one hyperactive wallet can't flood the file.

boring_no.why: 2026-11-10 winners.py (backtest/winners.md, Jan: 'build both'): replayed as a rule on finished markets (first time No is at 90-97c with 30+ days left, next real $100+ buy +1c + fee), topic 'other' made +$5.45 per $100 on 101 bets (100 won), ahead in all 11 months; exam verdict 'Promising, needs more bets', worst case -$0.75. Found by looking at 282 kinds of bet. Also registered for the 2026-12-21 holdout (PROTOCOL.md). Claude's track, rule changes reported.
boring_no.max_over_listed_note: Skip when the real ask is 2c+ above the listed price: the replay allowed fills at most 2c outside the band.

crypto_no.why: 2026-11-10 winners.py (backtest/winners.md, Jan: 'build both'): replayed as a rule on finished markets (first time No is at 70-90c with 3-7 days left, next real $100+ buy +1c + fee), crypto price markets made +$6.95 per $100 on 115 bets (102 won), ahead in all 9 months; the same bet on Yes lost. Exam verdict 'Ahead, but could be luck'. Found by looking at 282 kinds of bet. Also registered for the 2026-12-21 holdout (PROTOCOL.md). Claude's track, rule changes reported.
crypto_no.max_over_listed_note: Skip when the real ask is 2c+ above the listed price: the replay allowed fills at most 2c outside the band.

soccer_draw.why: 2026-11-10 census + digs (census.py, digs.py, backtest/census.md, digs_draws.md): soccer full-time draws at 15-50c bought 24h before kickoff made +$5.60 per $100 at +2c over 4,538 games (worst case +$1.70), gone at +4c. Pre-registered for the 21 Dec holdout as soccer_draw (PROTOCOL 5). Jan said Go for a $50 live paper track (2026-11-10). Claude's track, rule changes reported.
soccer_draw.max_over_listed_note: The lead is only about 2c, so skip when the real ask is 3c+ above the listed price.

word_no.why: 2026-11-13 mentions.py (backtest/mentions.md, new-strategy thread, Jan said go 13 Nov): 24,228 finished mention markets. Since April 2026 (when blind 'always No' stopped paying), buying No where Yes traded 20c+ above the word's own record with that speaker (3+ earlier markets) made +$15.25 per $100 on 533 bets at the worst price of the next 5 minutes + 3c + fee (exam: Promising, needs more bets). Same rule without word knowledge about $0. Weak spots: no untouched test set, +$7.74 at +5c cost, $0 at +8c, June and August lost, bets in the last 6 hours lose. Buying Yes loses. UNTESTED live. Claude's track, rule changes reported.
word_no.min_gap_note: Listed Yes price minus the word's own record must be 20c or more.
word_no.min_hist_note: The speaker needs 3 or more earlier finished markets with this word.
word_no.min_model_edge_note: After the real asking price and the fee, No must still be 10c under the record's chance (same bar as the history test).
word_no.max_over_listed_note: Skip when the real ask is 5c+ above the listed price (thin book): the history lead is about gone at +8c.
word_no.min_hours_to_end_note: In the history, bets in the last 6 hours before the listed end lost.

stock_no.why: 2026-11-13 stocks.py comb (backtest/stocks_comb.md, new-strategy thread, Jan picked 'Yes, $100 paper track' 13 Nov): about 150 price-only cuts on 14,506 finished stock price markets. Buying Yes loses almost everywhere (long shots $25-90 per $100). The other side, No where Yes last traded at 5-25c with 4 and 2 hours left before the close, made +$5.33 per $100 on 339 bets (corrected 13 Nov: 33 of those bets bought No under 70c, prices the live track never takes, and made half the profit; the 254 bets bought at 75-95c, like the live track, made +$2.60 per $100, exam verdict Ahead, but could be luck) at the worst price of the next 15 minutes + 2c + fee (exam: Promising, needs more bets), but -$5.58 at the worst price of the next 2 hours, and it was behind at the open and in the last hour. Trade history can't say what a buyer really pays in these thin markets, so this track buys only at real asks close to the listed price. UNTESTED live. Claude's track, rule changes reported.
stock_no.min_yes_note: Listed Yes price must be 5c to under 25c: the long shots people overpay for.
stock_no.hours_note: History: ahead with 4 and 2 hours left, behind just after the open and in the last hour.
stock_no.max_over_listed_note: Skip when the real ask for No is 3c+ above the listed price: the history lead is +$3 at 4c of extra cost and gone at the harsher price.

postcount_no.why: 2026-11-12 tweets.py (backtest/tweets.md, new-strategy thread): on 216 finished count windows (3,267 markets), checked every 30 minutes and bought at the next real trade + 1c + fee, buying No where Yes was 10c+ above a simple counting model made +$4.16 per $100 on 825 bets (exam: Promising, needs more bets). Weak spots: +$1.53 on the windows opened later, Elon alone +$1.57, gone at +3c cost. Buying Yes and betting both sides lost. No under 10c is excluded (one 2c lottery ticket made half the unfiltered profit). UNTESTED live. Claude's track, rule changes reported.
postcount_no.min_gap_note: Listed Yes price minus the counter's chance must be 10c or more.
postcount_no.min_model_edge_note: After the real asking price and the fee, No must still be 7c under the counter's chance (10c gap minus up to 2c of slip and about 1c of fee).
postcount_no.max_over_listed_note: Skip when the real ask is 2c+ above the listed price: the history test dies at +3c.

quiet_no.why: 2026-11-09 idea machine (ideas.py, backtest/ideas.md): on whole events, markets whose price moved under 2c in the last 7 days, NO at 50-75c bought 1-3 days before the end, made +$25 / +$35 per $100 at +2c in the two halves (+$23 at +5c, 153 events), passing a 33,823-idea screen with a many-ideas correction; no placebo passed. Replayed as a bot would enter (first qualifying hour, btcheck.quiet_bets): +$0.32 per $100 at +2c over 215 events, second half negative, so it was dropped as a research lead; Jan chose (2026-11-09) to run it live on $50 paper anyway. Not in PROTOCOL.md's holdout table. Claude's track, rule changes reported.
quiet_no.max_over_listed_note: Skip when the real ask is 5c+ above the listed price (thin book).

mention_no.why: 2026-11-09 calibration hunt (calib.py, backtest/calib.md): in 89 finished 'will X say Y' events, buying YES at 10-90c lost about $30 per $100 and buying NO won about $15 per $100 at +2c slippage, in both halves of the period. Fans overrate the chance of a given word. Claude's track, rule changes reported.
mention_no.max_over_listed_note: Skip when the real ask is 5c+ above the listed price (thin book). Live dry run 2026-11-09: one listed 26c asked 47c.

fade_sure.why: 2026-11-08: 'sure' 93-98c favorites in weather/crypto-price/post-count markets a day before the end flipped far more often than their price said (backtest/report.md). This buys the other side. Checked with backtest.py btfade (backtest/fade.md). From the Reddit/forum idea hunt; Claude's track, rule changes reported.
fade_sure.only_words_note: Weather only: in backtest/fade.md crypto-price and post-count buckets came out about even at +1c and lost at +2c.

econ_fav.why: 2026-11-09 econ.py backtest (backtest/econ.md): on 340 Kalshi data releases 2021-2026, buying the 80-99c side when the forecast said it was worth 3c+ more made +$6.73 per $100 24h before (141 bets, 7 lost) and +$7.75 72h before, both halves ahead, still ahead 2c worse; the same band without the forecast lost about $5 per $100. Found after looking at price bands, so the live track is the real test. Claude's track, rule changes reported.

kalshi_patient.why: 2026-11-12 khouse.py (backtest/khouse.md): 19,385 settled Kalshi markets, 3.2 million real trades. A patient buyer loses on slow questions, weather, crypto and stocks at most prices and badly in live sports (picked off). Only the nearly-sure side (best buy order 90-97c) was ahead in the two samples it was found in (+$1.42 per $100 on 971 bets); on a fresh third sample it was behind (-$1.99 on 304). All three: +$0.61 per $100, luck range -$0.60 to +$1.82, exam verdict 'Ahead, but could be luck'. Hourly orders like the backtest. Claude's track, rule changes reported; pass bar locked in PROTOCOL.md 5d (Jan's OK, 12 Nov). $1,000 because 40 waiting orders ($400) plus bets held up to a week need room; the scoreboard shows the most money ever tied up.

sharp_pinnacle.why: Jan's idea (2026-11-09): Pinnacle is the bookie the pros bet with, so its odds minus its margin are a strong fair price. Polymarket market makers mostly copy Pinnacle, so gaps should be rare and short; this measures how often a 15-minute bot catches one. Fair = the lower of two de-vig methods (sharp.py). One bet per game. Claude's track, rule changes reported.
sharp_pinnacle.sports_note: Tennis left out: retirement rules differ between Pinnacle and Polymarket.

wx_forecast.why: Weather specialists are among Polymarket's steadiest earners, and a 51-member ensemble corrected to the station is a real forecasting edge over a thin crowd. Settles on hourly METAR reports, so what's observed so far today is fixed. One bet per city-day.

crypto_late.why: Endgame with live data: near the close, a coin that is well past the strike rarely comes back. Volatility is inflated 1.5x so a sudden jump is priced in. Hourly candles give many chances a day.
